parties: President of India (Ministry of Railways) | Indian Railway Finance Corporation Limited
headline: Indian Railway Finance Corporation Limited: Offer for sale — Government exercises over-subscription option
sum: The Ministry of Railways has notified the NSE of its intention to exercise an over-subscription option to sell 11.24 crore equity shares in Indian Railway Finance Corporation Limited. This represents a secondary offer by the sovereign shareholder following an earlier primary issuance.
detail: The Government of India, via the Ministry of Railways, has formally communicated to NSE its decision to invoke an over-subscription clause relating to 11,24,02,040 (11.24 crore) equity shares in IRFC. The transaction appears to be a secondary offering mechanism (likely a follow-on public offer or stake-sale tranche). Over-subscription mechanics typically allow the issuer to allot additional shares beyond the initial tranche if demand exceeds supply. The exact pricing, timeline for settlement, and regulatory approvals (SEBI for OFS rules, CCI if anti-competitive concerns arise, and DIPAM for disinvestment norms) will determine final structure.

NSE/BSE listing rules compliance for secondary market trading post-allotment
CCI anti-competitive clearance (if threshold for notification crossed)
Depositories and settlement finality under the Depositories Act
approvals: NSE/BSE exchange approval/notification (completed — evidenced by NSE filing)
SEBI OFS framework approval (implicit in exchange notification)
DIPAM/Ministry of Railways internal clearance for disinvestment exercise
Potential CCI notification (if material change in control or ownership concentration)
structure.novel: Government exercise of over-subscription option in a public listed NBFC is administratively routine but regulatory-heavy; the novelty lies in the scale (11.24 cr shares) and the coordinated multi-regulator gate (SEBI, CCI, DIPAM). Structure suggests a carefully staged exit rather than a single block trade.

triggers.note: Mandatory disclosure and adherence to OFS pricing and settlement rules; government must publish offer document.
If the OFS results in a >40% stake acquisition/divestment by or to any party, CCI notification/approval mandatory.
All equity shares must be held in dematerialized form and settled via NSDL/CDSL; settlement finality on T+2.
IRFC must immediately disclose the OFS and over-subscription decision to both exchanges (material event).
Government's OFS execution must follow budgetary, transparency, and use-of-proceeds norms.
